figures_added.what: Pie chart with a 72 degree Science sector (soft blue) and 288 degree Other sector, labelled 'Science 72 deg'. Matches the 200-student / 72 deg problem text.
Four-sector pie: 120, 80, 60 degrees labelled, plus the unknown fourth sector marked '?'. Sectors sum to 360; the ? marks exactly what is asked.
Pie chart with Sector A at 96 degrees (soft blue) and 264 degree Other, labelled 'A 96 deg'. Matches the 150-people / 96 deg problem.

Two side-by-side pie charts: School A with a 90 degree football sector (title 'School A (200)') and School B with a 60 degree football sector (title 'School B (300)'). Both football fan counts resolve to 50, matching the comparison problem.

notes: The opener and all three teach walks describe a figure, so each carries an inline SVG per the show-what-you-say rule: opener = a circle split into two equal halves (Football / Other); teach.bronze = a four-bar bar chart (Cats 14, Dogs 22, Fish 6, Birds 8) with axis, gridlines and value labels; teach.silver = a pie with a 54 degree Tea sector; teach.gold = a single stacked bar (Books 30 / Toys 10 / Games 10). All SVGs are theme-safe: text and outline strokes use currentColor, region fills use soft colours at fill-opacity 0.35, Inter labels, viewBox + role='img' + aria-label, self-contained, each under 1.5KB. The 12 problems that already carried Chart.js configs (bar / scatter / line / pie) were left unchanged. Every visible figure number was cross-checked against its problem text and solution.
